fluff.overview:
The Super-Wasp was an experimental twenty-five ton BattleMech developed in 3020 as a joint project between the New Avalon Institute of Science and Team Banzai. Building upon knowledge recovered from the Halstead Station cache, the project aimed to fully rebuild and redesign the proven Wasp chassis using experimental technologies. The hand-built prototype represented an ambitious attempt to create a superior reconnaissance platform that exceeded the capabilities of the original design.

Featuring thirty percent more armor than the standard Wasp and double the laser firepower, the Super-Wasp also incorporated an experimental supercharger capable of providing brief bursts of exceptional speed. However, the project never progressed beyond the prototype stage, with both constructed examples destroyed during a raid on Hoff in 3022.
fluff.capabilities:
The Super-Wasp mounted an enhanced armament consisting of two Diverse Optics Type 2 medium lasers in the arm, doubling the firepower of the standard Wasp while maintaining the all-energy weapons philosophy that minimized logistics requirements. The additional five tons of mass over the original design allowed for thirty percent more armor protection, addressing one of the base chassis's most significant weaknesses.

The most innovative feature was the experimental supercharger, which enabled bursts of speed comparable to myomer accelerator signal circuitry. This system gave the Super-Wasp exceptional sprint capability for disengaging from threats or rapidly repositioning on the battlefield. However, the technology carried significant risk, as extensive use could cause catastrophic engine damage.

Despite these improvements, the Super-Wasp remained a prototype design with inherent limitations. The supercharger's unreliability and the chassis's experimental nature meant it was unsuitable for mass production with the technology available during the early thirty-first century. The hand-built construction also prevented economical scaling of the design.
fluff.history:
The Super-Wasp project began in 3020 at the Friden Aerospace Park on Hoff under the supervision of Dr. Jorge Belasco. The initiative represented one of several NAIS efforts to leverage recovered Star League technology for practical military applications. Two Super-Wasp prototypes were constructed alongside a Super Griffin as proof-of-concept demonstrators for the experimental technologies involved.

On 13 May 3022, the prototypes received an unexpected baptism of fire when House Kurita forces and Wolf's Dragoons raided Hoff. Deployed as a last line of defense for the research facility, the Super-Wasps demonstrated both the potential and limitations of the experimental design. One prototype disabled a Dragoons Stinger before suffering catastrophic engine damage when its supercharger failed, leaving it vulnerable to the elite Black Widow Company. The second Super-Wasp destroyed an enemy Phoenix Hawk before an ammunition explosion destroyed it completely.

Though both prototypes were lost, their sacrifice bought sufficient time for Davion scientists to evacuate most personnel and critical research data. The unusual circumstances of the engagement led to conflicting reports and exaggerated rumors about the prototypes' capabilities. House Kurita claimed both pilots survived and were eventually ransomed back to House Davion. The Super-Wasp project was not revived, as the experimental technologies proved too unreliable for practical deployment with early thirty-first century manufacturing capabilities.
fluff.deployment: The sole Super-Wasp variant, this variant mounted twin medium lasers, enhanced armor protection, and an experimental supercharger system. Two prototypes were constructed at Friden Aerospace Park on Hoff before the facility was raided in 3022. Both examples were destroyed defending the research complex against Wolf's Dragoons and House Kurita forces, though their sacrifice allowed evacuation of critical personnel and data. The experimental technologies proved too unreliable for production with contemporary manufacturing capabilities.
